Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary and for the spreadsheet. Appreciate the traffic samples — they make sizing straightforward. High-level proposal and next steps below (happy to hop on a short call to finalize).

Baseline reserved capacity (POC):
- Reserve 4x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs (steady-state). This covers your stated concurrency for the chat workload with room for the embedding batch.

Autoscaling / burst plan:
- Autoscale policy: scale-up increments of 4 GPUs, max burst to 16 GPUs.
- Pre-warm pool: maintain 2 warm instances to reduce cold-starts during burst events. Pre-warm will be billed at a reduced rate but keeps KV caches warm for your model family.
- Scale latency: warm scaling targets ~30-60s to be fully operational (we can also pre-schedule test bursts to pre-warm).

Expected performance and cost notes:
- Target: p95 latency < 150ms for the baseline config on latest optimized FP16 kernels (subject to final model choice).
- If you want guaranteed 100ms p95 we should discuss slightly larger reserved footprint or model variants optimized for latency.

Ownership & runbook:
- Redwood owner for provisioning: dev_patel (cc'd) - will create the reserved pool and set autoscale policy.
- Tech contact on your side: Raj (cc'd) and ops@venturotech for cloud-side network/Security checks.
- Fallback: we will configure automatic fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized model if latency or capacity issues occur. We'll keep the same API contract.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (by Aug 2): Provision reserved pool and baseline test harness.
- Week 1: End-to-end onboarding, data ingest, basic quality checks.
- Weeks 2-5: Evaluation window (metrics collection, cost/latency monitoring).

Success criteria (proposal):
1) p95 generation latency < 200ms on baseline workload and <150ms on optimized runs.
2) Eval accuracy within 5% of your baseline across the 3 eval suites.
3) No outages affecting >5% of requests during evaluation window.

Next steps:
- I will share a brief proposal PDF and a HubSpot playbook with the POC plan.
- dev_patel to provision reserved GPUs and confirm scheduled pre-warm windows.
- Raj/Alice to confirm start date (Aug 2) and sign the POC order form.

Thanks Raj — good questions. Answers below and a few action items so we can hit Aug 2: 

1) Billing during bursts:
- Bursts (autoscaled capacity beyond reserved pool) are billed at our on-demand rate which is ~1.4x the reserved unit price. We'll include a sample cost model in the proposal PDF. For transparency we'll instrument per-GPU token-level cost and share daily burn reports.

2) Pre-warm pool cache isolation:
- Pre-warm instances will be assigned to your tenant only for the POC. KV cache and any cache-layering will be isolated to VenturoTech model versions - no cross-tenant sharing.

3) Cold-start latency (from zero):
- Cold-start to fully ready (model load + kernel JIT + KV warm) is typically 90-180s depending on model size. With pre-warm we expect this to be <10s for most requests.

Provisioning details (internal action items):
- dev_patel: please provision 4x A100-80GB-equivalent reserved units in our us-west cluster, configure autoscale increments of 4 up to 16, and add a 2-instance pre-warm pool for the VenturoTech POC. Include cost-logging hooks and token-level attribution.
- marcus_lin: please prepare a runbook for fallback (quantized variant + graceful degrade path) and a short smoke test checklist we can run after provisioning.

Docs & attachments:
- Attached is the Redwood POC proposal (redwood_proposal_v2.pdf) with the cost model and SLA bullets.
- HubSpot deal page is linked for signature and to attach the PO.

Final ask from VenturoTech: please confirm Aug 2 as the POC start, and Ops to confirm that the network changes (VPC peering, firewall rules) can be completed by Jul 30.
